claims.title: Portuguese reach the uninhabited islands
claims.summary: Sailing for Prince Henry the Navigator, the Venetian captain Alvise Cadamosto and others made landfall on the empty Cape Verde archipelago; further islands were charted over the next decade by Diogo Gomes and António de Noli.

sources.label: The Portuguese Colonization of Cape Verde

claims.title: Ribeira Grande founded on Santiago
claims.summary: Portuguese settlers established Ribeira Grande (today Cidade Velha) on Santiago — the first permanent European city in the tropics — drawing Portuguese, Genoese and Flemish settlers, convicts and Sephardic Jews.

sources.label: Cidade Velha, Historic Centre of Ribeira Grande

claims.title: Trading privileges over the Guinea coast
claims.summary: The Portuguese crown granted Santiago's settlers the right to trade in the "Rivers of Guinea" on the West African mainland, anchoring the colony's economy to commerce with the coast.

sources.label: The Portuguese Colonization of Cape Verde

claims.title: The Nossa Senhora do Rosário church
claims.summary: Construction of the church of Nossa Senhora do Rosário at Ribeira Grande, among the oldest surviving colonial churches anywhere, reflected the town's new role as a bishopric and religious centre of the islands.

sources.label: Cidade Velha, Historic Centre of Ribeira Grande

claims.title: A sorting-house of the slave trade
claims.summary: Ribeira Grande became a major entrepôt where enslaved Africans from the Upper Guinea coast were held, baptised, taxed and re-exported to the Americas, with thousands passing through annually by mid-century.

sources.label: The Portuguese Colonization of Cape Verde

claims.title: Drake sacks Ribeira Grande
claims.summary: The English privateer Sir Francis Drake attacked and sacked the wealthy port of Ribeira Grande, one of several corsair raids that beset the islands during the era of the Iberian Union.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1585-drake-sacks-ribeira-grande, claim TL:CPV:event:1585:drake-sacks-ribeira-grande, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cassard's French raid destroys the city
claims.summary: The French corsair Jacques Cassard stormed and looted Ribeira Grande, stripping its churches and houses; the coastal town, already declining, never recovered from the assault.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1712-cassard-s-french-raid-destroys-the-city, claim TL:CPV:event:1712:cassard-s-french-raid-destroys-the-city, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capital moves to Praia
claims.summary: As the slave trade waned and Ribeira Grande lay in ruins, administration shifted to the more defensible plateau of Praia, which became the capital in 1770 and remains so today.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1770-capital-moves-to-praia, claim TL:CPV:event:1770:capital-moves-to-praia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mindelo becomes an Atlantic coaling station
claims.summary: The deep harbour of Porto Grande at Mindelo on São Vicente was developed as a coaling station for transatlantic steamships and later a submarine-cable relay, briefly making the port cosmopolitan and prosperous.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1839-mindelo-becomes-an-atlantic-coaling-station, claim TL:CPV:event:1839:mindelo-becomes-an-atlantic-coaling-station, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slavery abolished
claims.summary: Portugal abolished slavery in its territories in 1869, ending the legal trade that had built the islands' early wealth, though forced and contract labour systems persisted afterward.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1869-slavery-abolished, claim TL:CPV:event:1869:slavery-abolished, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Famines kill at least 100,000
claims.summary: Recurrent droughts produced a series of catastrophic famines; during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries at least 100,000 people died of starvation and disease, amid an inadequate colonial response.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1900-famines-kill-at-least-100-000, claim TL:CPV:event:1900:famines-kill-at-least-100-000, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The twentieth-century famines
claims.summary: Two further droughts brought famines that together killed tens of thousands; starving refugees were interned in camps outside Praia, and survivors emigrated in growing numbers, deepening the diaspora.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1947-the-twentieth-century-famines, claim TL:CPV:event:1947:the-twentieth-century-famines, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The morna and Creole letters
claims.summary: The poet Eugénio Tavares of Brava elevated the morna to a literary art in Cape Verdean Creole; the song-form of love, parting and sodade would later be carried worldwide by Cesária Évora.

claims.title: Cabral founds the PAIGC
claims.summary: Amílcar Cabral and a small group founded the African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde, conceiving the two Portuguese territories as one nation to be liberated together.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1956-cabral-founds-the-paigc, claim TL:CPV:event:1956:cabral-founds-the-paigc, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Armed struggle begins on the mainland
claims.summary: Because the islands were unsuited to guerrilla war, the PAIGC waged its armed campaign on the Guinea-Bissau mainland from 1963, while Cape Verdean cadres filled the party's leadership.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1963-armed-struggle-begins-on-the-mainland, claim TL:CPV:event:1963:armed-struggle-begins-on-the-mainland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cabral assassinated in Conakry
claims.summary: Amílcar Cabral was shot dead at a PAIGC roadblock in Conakry by a party member and others, in a plot widely linked to Portuguese agents, two years before the islands gained independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1973-cabral-assassinated-in-conakry, claim TL:CPV:event:1973:cabral-assassinated-in-conakry, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Carnation Revolution
claims.summary: A military coup in Lisbon overthrew Portugal's Estado Novo dictatorship, worn down by its colonial wars, opening the way to decolonisation and negotiations on Cape Verde's independence.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Cabo Verde

claims.title: Independence of Cape Verde
claims.summary: The Republic of Cape Verde declared independence from Portugal on 5 July 1975 under the PAIGC, with Aristides Pereira as first president; the United States recognised the new state the same day.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Cabo Verde

claims.title: Bissau coup ends the union
claims.summary: A coup in Guinea-Bissau led by João Bernardo "Nino" Vieira overthrew President Luís Cabral and shattered the planned union with Cape Verde, whose PAIGC branch broke away to form the separate PAICV.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1980-bissau-coup-ends-the-union, claim TL:CPV:event:1980:bissau-coup-ends-the-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The PAICV and a one-party state
claims.summary: Cape Verde's branch of the PAIGC was reconstituted as the African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde (PAICV), which governed the islands as a pragmatic one-party state through the 1980s.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1981-the-paicv-and-a-one-party-state, claim TL:CPV:event:1981:the-paicv-and-a-one-party-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: End of one-party rule
claims.summary: Amid rising pressure for pluralism, the opposition Movement for Democracy (MpD) formed in April 1990 and the National Assembly abolished single-party rule that September, clearing the way for free elections.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1990-end-of-one-party-rule, claim TL:CPV:event:1990:end-of-one-party-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First multiparty elections
claims.summary: In Cape Verde's first free elections the MpD won a parliamentary majority, and António Mascarenhas Monteiro defeated President Aristides Pereira with about 73 per cent of the vote; the PAICV ceded power peacefully.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-1991-first-multiparty-elections, claim TL:CPV:event:1991:first-multiparty-elections, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Peaceful alternation of power
claims.summary: The PAICV returned to government in the 2001 elections and Pedro Pires won the presidency, confirming a pattern of peaceful, competitive transfers of power between rival parties.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cape Verde: From uninhabited mid-Atlantic islands and the first European town in the tropics, through the Atlantic slave trade, recurring famine and a distinctive Creole culture, to Amílcar Cabral's liberation struggle, independence in 1975, and one of Africa's most stable democracies.", terralore.co/country/CPV/chronicle#ev-2001-peaceful-alternation-of-power, claim TL:CPV:event:2001:peaceful-alternation-of-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cesária Évora and morna go global
claims.summary: Cesária Évora, the "barefoot diva", won a Grammy for the album Voz d'Amor, the high point of a career that carried Cape Verdean morna and its Creole longing to audiences worldwide.

claims.title: Graduation from least-developed status
claims.summary: Buoyed by tourism, remittances and stable governance, Cape Verde graduated from the UN list of least-developed countries — a rare achievement for an African state — confirming its development progress.

claims.title: Cidade Velha named a World Heritage Site
claims.summary: UNESCO inscribed Cidade Velha, the Historic Centre of Ribeira Grande — the first European city in the tropics — as Cape Verde's only World Heritage Site, recognising its role in the Atlantic slave trade and colonial expansion.
